thread:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: model warmup failures in us-west-2 cluster — repeated OOMs and deserialization errors. Auto-escalating and creating incident channel #inc-1748001111

SRE-ONCALL: I'm on it, paging infra and runtime. Starting triage.

ml-runtime: seeing a bunch of `load_model()` failures: `deser: invalid header` then crash OOM when allocating KV cache. Sample error below:
```
2026-03-15T10:05:12Z ERROR model_warmup: deser: invalid magic (artifact v3)
2026-03-15T10:05:12Z INFO model_warmup: retrying load (attempt 1)
2026-03-15T10:05:13Z ERROR runtime: OOM allocating 5.2GiB for kv_cache
2026-03-15T10:05:13Z WARN k8s: container restart loop (exit 137)
```

eng-infra: nodes in the affected nodepool are flapping, kubelet reports `eviction threshold crossed` and `OOMKilled` on the container. No disk pressure.

support: @sre-oncall can we surface which customers are failing? Ops reports 3 active customer routes with increased 502s.

sre-oncall: confirmed 3 customers in us-west region, degraded 95th token latency and increased error rates. Currently routing fallback not triggered for some because model pinned.

alice: trying an immediate mitigation: marking model variant `v1-small` as fallback and enabling route-level fallback to reduce memory pressure. Applying now.

ml-runtime: patching rollout to prefer `v1-small` for the affected routes, also toggled `enable_prefix_cache=false` for warmup jobs to reduce mem.

eng-infra: cordoning two nodes to stop scheduling new warmups, draining a node to let pods reschedule onto healthier hosts.

charlie: starting a targeted restart of warmup service with `--max-concurrency=1` to avoid simultaneous heavy loads. Also increasing ephemeral swap on hosts as temporary buffer (see playbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/warmup-oom).

support: notifying the three affected customers: "We're seeing transient model warmup issues causing increased errors; mitigation in progress, reduced impact expected within ~30m." Will update when fallback completes.

oncall-manager: If fallback reduces errors, coordinate a postmortem and decide whether to revert pinning or change warmup sizing defaults. Good work. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: handoff to charlie for monitoring and follow-ups — I'm stepping out for an overlapping pager rotation. charlie, you have the channel.

charlie: taking over. Current status: fallbacks applied, node cordon/drain in flight, mem pressure dropping on new pods. Will monitor for 30m.

ml-runtime: additional note — compile-timeouts observed for one model variant earlier (linking logs) but those stopped after we disabled concurrent compilation. We should consider increasing compile timeout for artifact v3 in future config.

charlie: tracking metrics: 502s reduced from 7% -> 1.2% since fallback, 95p latency down ~45%. Keeping channel open.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, customer impact reduced, oncall: charlie (handed off).

charlie: will start a short RCA timeline: collect warmup logs, artifact checksums, node-level memory graphs, and any recent infra changes. Planning blameless postmortem if we confirm systemic issue.

support: sent customer follow-up: "Mitigation applied; we'll confirm when stable and share root cause."

charlie: closing loop for now — continued monitoring. If errors resurge, escalate to eng-runtime and SRE lead.

alice: quick follow-up: we'll add a temporary guard in the autoscaler to avoid simultaneous model warmup blasts on the same nodepool. Filing a RFC ticket after incident: https://redwood.internal/boards/ISSUE-1723

oncall-manager: great. Ensure the postmortem captures the interaction between deserialization failures and warmup concurrency.

charlie: acknowledged. last update: reduced errors, no new OOMs in last 10m. Leaving channel open for another 20m then will mark incident as mitigated. :white_check_mark:
